clue.text: Alarm about start of disease, emergency measures widely affecting population

indicators.note: about here means the word for alarm goes round the other letters

parts.note: alarm is panic, a sudden fright

indicators.note: the start of each of the three words disease, emergency, measures is taken

explanation.surface: Health officials rush in emergency measures as fear of a spreading disease grips the population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' covers all three of the words after it, not only 'disease', so 'emergency measures' supplies two letters instead of being part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak spread across a whole country or the world, hitting a broad share of people.

clue.text: A loop with hook I removed from a long-necked creature

indicators.note: removed from says the letter I is taken out of the creature's name

parts.note: the giraffe is the animal famous for its long neck
taken as written

explanation.surface: A zookeeper unhooks a loop from a giraffe's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' that opens the definition is also 'a' in the wordplay: the clue's 'a long-necked creature' gives A plus GIRAFFE less I.
explanation.definitionFit: An agraffe is a clasp or fastening made of a hook and an eye, used on armour and clothing.

definitions.meaning: to assume clothing is to put it on
a university teacher at Oxford or Cambridge is called a ...

explanation.surface: Someone takes for granted that a man is a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a garment is to assume it, and a college fellow or tutor is a don.

clue.text: Minor university, not class, I claim, camouflaging these blunders

indicators.note: camouflaging means disguising the letters by mixing them up

parts.note: a minor, small letter u stands for university
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small college insists it is not about class, while hiding its mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camouflaging' scrambles U with NOTCLASS and ICLAIM, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscalculations are errors of judgement or arithmetic, mistakes of the kind called blunders.

parts.note: a firm is a company, CO, and firms plural gives two of them
the second company abbreviation

explanation.surface: Businesses linked to the drinks trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Not just swings and roundabouts topping fellow produces

indicators.note: topping means removing the top, here the first letter

parts.note: swings and roundabouts are rides found at a funfair

explanation.surface: Life's ups and downs strike someone as unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swings and roundabouts' is a British idiom for gains balancing losses; here it is literal fairground rides. 'topping' cuts the F (fellow) off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust is lacking fairness, the opposite of equitable.

clue.text: One chump grinned in embarrassment — not having a clue

indicators.note: in embarrassment suggests the letters are thrown into confusion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool grins sheepishly, completely baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a clue means failing to grasp or understand anything.

clue.text: Trip, crossing under street — display of bloomers!

indicators.note: crossing here means the word for trip spans the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to trip is to stumble and fall
under means lower, as in a lower position

explanation.surface: Someone trips crossing an underpass and shows their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowers, and a stall displays them.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist's stand on a street shows off flowers, things that bloom, for sale.

clue.text: It's me that's struggling to be specific

indicators.note: struggling suggests letters writhing about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are having trouble being precise.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one, giving details rather than generalities.

clue.text: Makes an effort to see demoiselles

definitions.meaning: stretches the neck out to get a view
the demoiselle is a small species of long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone strains to catch sight of young ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demoiselles' looks like young women, but the demoiselle is also a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Craning is stretching one's neck to look, and the demoiselle is a kind of crane bird.

indicators.note: skirt means go round the edge of, so the cycles surround the other letters

parts.note: bicycles are cycles, vehicles with two wheels
ahead means on, forward, as in go on

explanation.surface: Cyclists ride round bad weather lying ahead of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' gives ON, as in pressing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclones are violent rotating weather systems, severe storms.

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A precious old reel of film has been ruined, a cautionary tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or siren that sounds to alert people to a blaze is a warning.

clue.text: Rolling out barrel, drew last ale for a bird

indicators.note: rolling out suggests the letters tumble about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of ale is taken

explanation.surface: A publican rolls out a cask and pours the last of the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling out' rearranges BARREL, DREW and E (the last letter of 'ale').
explanation.definitionFit: The reed warbler is a small brown songbird of reedbeds.

indicators.note: bringing back means the fruit is read in reverse

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A lad returns with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a male first name, as in Emil and the Detectives.

clue.text: North American Indian people — the last on earth

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a fox's earth is its burrow or den

indicators.note: the last letter of the is taken

explanation.surface: An Indigenous people are imagined as the final ones left on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' is not the planet but a fox's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dene are an Athabaskan-speaking First Nations group of northern Canada.

clue.text: Key order news media's top journalist abridged

parts.note: C is a musical key
OM is the Order of Merit
the press is the news media
an editor, ED, is the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A leading editor cuts a story from the press.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been shortened or squeezed into less space is condensed.

indicators.note: that's of says the plant is part of the following words, its letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A plant that has some practical value.
explanation.definitionFit: Meu, also called spignel or baldmoney, is an aromatic umbelliferous herb.

clue.text: Vehicle at present parking in a bog

indicators.note: in means the other letters sit inside the word for bog

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog
at present means now

explanation.surface: A car is currently parked in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowplough is a vehicle with a blade for clearing roads after snowfall.

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A naval officer clambering up again takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the great waterfall on the US-Canada border.

indicators.note: rocky means unstable, shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Trees are spotted on a stony mountain route.
explanation.definitionFit: Asp is an old name for the aspen, a poplar tree with trembling leaves.

parts.note: pa is dad, so dad's is pa's
a period is a time

explanation.surface: A father's spell of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby or leisure activity, something done for fun.

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A soft melody or a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple of matching things, a brace or duo.

indicators.note: made from says new letters are formed by rearranging the following words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Homemade musical instruments are fashioned out of big cans.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a percussion instrument, a steel bar bent into three sides.

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a point of contention
offspring, as in died without children

explanation.surface: Parents argue over custody of their kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A contested point is an issue, and legally offspring are a person's issue.

clue.text: Dances around naked? Glasses are called for!

definitions.meaning: burlesque dances where a nude performer hides behind inflated bags
brandy snifters with large round bowls are called by this name

explanation.surface: Someone dances in the nude, and it is time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the burlesque balloon dance, where a naked dancer is screened by inflated globes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated rubber globes screen a nude dancer, and big-bowled brandy snifters share the name.

parts.note: taken as written
a grid is a framework of bars

explanation.surface: A young woman joins a gym and does some bar exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a female given name, as in the actress Ingrid Bergman.

parts.note: G is short for great, as in G for grand
A is a top grade in exams

explanation.surface: A splendid first-class river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted predatory fish, also called garfish.

definitions.meaning: a cloth woven in the Outer Hebrides, famous for tweed suits
one of the three men in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: A man in a tweed suit goes boating.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides that gives its name to a handwoven tweed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebridean island names a famous handwoven cloth, and Jerome's Thames boat party includes a character with that surname.

clue.text: Filled to excess, taking Cheddar, perhaps, in the end?

indicators.note: taking means the word for end takes in the other letters

parts.note: the end is an end
Cheddar Gorge is an example of a gorge, a steep ravine

explanation.surface: Someone has finally eaten too much Cheddar cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheddar' suggests cheese, but Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Engorged describes something swollen or gorged, crammed full beyond capacity.
